# Sirach 23 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 23 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 15

---

## Disagreement 001 — 23:1 prayer opening
**Verse:** 23:1
**EMET:** "do-not-abandon me to-their-counsel"
**LOGOS:** "do not abandon me to their counsel"
**PNEUMA:** "don't hand me over to what my mouth would do"
**Issue:** PNEUMA reinterprets "their counsel" as referring to the mouth's impulses rather than others' counsel. The Greek βουλῇ αὐτῶν — "their counsel" is ambiguous (whose counsel?). Context (continuation from ch. 22) suggests external adversaries or one's own impulses. PNEUMA's reading is possible but speculative.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "do not abandon me to their counsel" — retains the ambiguity of the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 002 — 23:2 "stripes / discipline" instrument metaphor
**Verse:** 23:2
**EMET:** "Who will-set stripes over my-thought"
**LOGOS:** "Who will set stripes over my thoughts"
**PNEUMA:** "I wish someone would discipline my thoughts the way a taskmaster disciplines a worker"
**Issue:** μαστιγώσῃ — "to whip/flog." EMET/LOGOS render literally. PNEUMA expands into a simile that interprets rather than translates. SOPHIA retains the direct metaphor.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Who will set stripes over my thoughts."

---

## Disagreement 003 — 23:4 "haughty-look / arrogant look / pride in eyes"
**Verse:** 23:4
**EMET:** "do-not-give to-me a-haughty-look"
**LOGOS:** "do not give me an arrogant look"
**PNEUMA:** "don't let pride take hold in my eyes"
**Issue:** ὑπερηφανίαν ὀφθαλμῶν — "pride of eyes." EMET and LOGOS render closely. PNEUMA paraphrases. SOPHIA follows LOGOS: "do not give me arrogant eyes."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "do not give me arrogant eyes."

---

## Disagreement 004 — 23:5 "desire-of-the-belly / desire for the belly / appetite"
**Verse:** 23:5
**EMET:** "desire-of-the-belly and of-intercourse"
**LOGOS:** "desire for the belly and for sexual intercourse"
**PNEUMA:** "appetite and sexual craving"
**Issue:** κοιλίας ὄρεξιν καὶ συνουσιασμόν — "appetite of the belly and sexual union." All three render the pair. PNEUMA's "sexual craving" is interpretive. SOPHIA uses "desire for food and for sexual union" to preserve the two-part structure without amplification.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Let not desire for food and for sexual union take hold of me."

---

## Disagreement 005 — 23:5 "shameless-soul / shameless soul / brazen spirit"
**Verse:** 23:5b
**EMET:** "a-shameless-soul"
**LOGOS:** "a shameless soul"
**PNEUMA:** "a brazen spirit"
**Issue:** ψυχῇ ἀναιδεῖ — "a shameless soul." "Spirit" for ψυχή is less precise. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a shameless spirit" — slight update to avoid "soul" being used twice differently in short space.

---

## Disagreement 006 — 23:8 "naming the Holy-One / naming the Holy One / mentioning God's holy name"
**Verse:** 23:8
**EMET:** "naming the-Holy-One"
**LOGOS:** "naming the Holy One"
**PNEUMA:** "mentioning God's holy name"
**Issue:** ὀνομάζειν τὸν ἅγιον — "to name the Holy One." This is a Jewish periphrasis for using the divine name. PNEUMA's paraphrase adds clarity but shifts from "the Holy One" as a divine title to "God's holy name."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "naming the Holy One" — preserving the divine title.

---

## Disagreement 007 — 23:9 "continually-examined / continually cross-examined / interrogated all the time"
**Verse:** 23:9
**EMET:** "a-slave who-is-continually-examined"
**LOGOS:** "a slave who is continually cross-examined"
**PNEUMA:** "A servant who gets interrogated all the time"
**Issue:** ἐξεταζόμενος διὰ παντός — "being continually examined/tested." LOGOS's "cross-examined" leans legal; EMET's "examined" is neutral; PNEUMA's "interrogated" is colloquial. SOPHIA: "continually questioned."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a slave who is continually questioned."

---

## Disagreement 008 — 23:11 "clothed-about with death / clothed about with death"
**Verse:** 23:11
**EMET:** "a-speech clothed-about with death"
**LOGOS:** "a mode of speech clothed about with death"
**PNEUMA:** "a way of speaking that is wrapped in death"
**Issue:** λόγος συγκεκαλυμμένος θανάτῳ — "a word/speech wrapped around with death." All three are defensible. SOPHIA follows LOGOS closely.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a manner of speech clothed about with death."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 23:11 "inheritance-of-Jacob" and its meaning
**Verse:** 23:11
**EMET/LOGOS:** "may it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob"
**PNEUMA:** "God forbid it should be found among the people of Jacob"
**Issue:** ἐν κληρονομίᾳ Ιακωβ — "in the inheritance of Jacob." PNEUMA loses "inheritance" for "people." The term "inheritance" has covenantal weight.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "the inheritance of Jacob" — retained.

---

## Disagreement 010 — 23:15 two/three types
**Verse:** 23:15
**EMET:** "Two types-of-persons multiply-sins, and a-third brings-on wrath"
**LOGOS:** "Two kinds of people multiply sins, and a third brings on wrath"
**PNEUMA:** "Two kinds of people pile sin on sin, and a third draws down God's anger"
**Issue:** The numerical pattern is a wisdom formula (cf. Prov 30). PNEUMA's "draws down God's anger" adds "God's" which is not in the Greek. All agents agree on the structure.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Two kinds of people multiply sins, and a third brings on wrath."

---

## Disagreement 011 — 23:17 divine omniscience affirmation
**Verse:** 23:18
**EMET:** "the-eyes of-the-LORD are ten-thousands-brighter than the-sun"
**LOGOS:** "the eyes of the LORD are ten thousand times brighter than the sun"
**PNEUMA:** "God's eyes are ten thousand times brighter than the sun"
**Issue:** κύριος — "LORD," not "God." PNEUMA substitutes "God's" for stylistic reasons. EMET/LOGOS preserve "LORD." This is a crucial theological affirmation; the divine name should be preserved.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "the eyes of the LORD are ten thousand times brighter than the sun."

---

## Disagreement 012 — 23:19 "All-things were-known before-they-were-created"
**Verse:** 23:19
**EMET:** "All-things were-known before-they-were-created, so-also after-they-were-completed"
**LOGOS:** "All things were known before they were created, and likewise after their completion"
**PNEUMA:** "Everything was known before it was made; everything is known after it's done"
**Issue:** πρὶν ἢ κτισθῆναι — "before being created." The theological weight is significant. All versions preserve the substance. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "All things were known before they were created, and likewise after they were completed."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 23:22 three counts against the adulteress
**Verse:** 23:22
**EMET:** "first / secondly / thirdly" structure
**LOGOS:** "first / secondly / and third" structure
**PNEUMA:** "First / Second / Third" (capitals) structure
**Issue:** All agents preserve the three-count structure. Minor formatting difference. SOPHIA follows LOGOS numbering format.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "first... second... and third."

---

## Disagreement 014 — 23:27 "great-honor / great glory / greatest honor"
**Verse:** 23:27
**EMET:** "A-great-honor it-is to-follow after-the-LORD"
**LOGOS:** "It is a great glory to follow the LORD"
**PNEUMA:** "Following the LORD is the greatest honor there is"
**Issue:** μεγάλη δόξα — "great glory." PNEUMA's superlative "greatest" is not in the Greek. LOGOS's "glory" is closer to δόξα than EMET's "honor."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "It is a great glory to follow after the LORD."

---

## Disagreement 015 — 23:28 textual status and content
**Verse:** 23:28
**EMET:** Brackets the verse as possibly secondary
**LOGOS:** Treats as part of the text ("will inherit glory")
**PNEUMA:** Treats as part of the text ("will inherit praise")
**Issue:** V. 28 is found in some MSS but missing in others. Content echoes earlier chapters. LOGOS uses "glory" (δόξαν); PNEUMA uses "praise." The Greek has δόξαν. SOPHIA includes the verse but notes its textual status. "Praise" for δόξα is unusual; "glory" is standard.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Whoever does these things will inherit praise" — follows PNEUMA here as "praise" fits the contextual parallelism with "fear of the LORD."
